title: Agent Artifacts may diverge freely from each other but must never constrain one another
content:
A.1.14.2.2 states both halves of the rule: "Agent Artifacts must not limit or constrain the effect or operation of other Agent Artifacts. Agents can freely experiment or pursue divergent governance and operational logic within their respective Artifacts, subject to the fundamental requirement that all Artifacts remain aligned with the Sky Core Atlas."

The structure is strictly two-dimensional. **Vertically**, every Artifact answers to the Sky Core Atlas. **Horizontally**, no Artifact has any authority over any other. A.1.14.2.1 completes the picture: "Subject to any relevant provisions in the Sky Core Atlas, Agents are governed by the provisions of their respective Agent Artifacts," which define strategic vision, day-to-day operational logic, and the processes Executor Agents must carry out.

The prohibition on horizontal constraint is what makes divergence safe. If Artifacts could bind each other, Agents would negotiate, form blocs, and accumulate cross-jurisdictional obligations — reproducing at Agent level exactly the entanglement the Scope partition exists to avoid, and creating a second power structure that does not answer to Sky Core.

The result is genuine parallel experimentation: incompatible governance designs can run simultaneously, each falsifiable on its own terms, with the Core Atlas as the only shared constraint. That is a real advantage over monolithic governance, where every change is global and every failure is systemic. The trade is redundancy and inconsistency across Agents — but that inconsistency is the price of being able to learn from more than one experiment at a time.
description: Horizontal non-interference plus vertical conformance: Agents can run incompatible governance experiments in parallel, provided each stays aligned with the Sky Core Atlas.
